page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-48-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs spanning 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with hyperthreading, the system features a 504 MB L3 cache alongside support for instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. It provides 180.0 GB of system memory, equating to 3.75 GB per vCPU, and integrates 3,216 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 8 drives. There are no GPUs attached to this instance.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong processing and memory throughput. The instance ranks in the top tier for single-core metrics, achieving 2,309.0 in Geekbench single-core, 37.09 GB/sec in gzip compression, and 15.63 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance is robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,360.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 70,646.91. Memory-intensive routines show cached small-block bandwidth reaching 3,861.88 GB/sec in the top 25%, while uncached large-block reads and writes register at 178.28 GB/sec and 71.33 GB/sec respectively.

Application tests reflect the utility of the bundled local NVMe storage and compute profile. Database operations scored 23,020.87 on PassMark, paired with 89.08 million Redis SET operations per second and 83.58 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference is also notable, generating 345.79 tokens per second on a small 135M model and 28.8 tokens per second on a 7B model.

By delivering dedicated Intel Xeon cores, a massive 504 MB L3 cache, and integrated NVMe SSD capacity, the c4-standard-48-lssd provides high resource density for I/O-intensive and low-latency workloads. It is appropriately suited for relational databases, NoSQL distributed data stores, large-scale software compilation, batch compression pipelines, and CPU-driven inference services.
